info.desc: In 1971, a year after the release of the critically-acclaimed yet commercially unsuccessful album Writer, an undaunted King gave thoughtful, folk-flavored reinterpretations of some of her early pop hits as a songwriter, interweaving them with new compositions in the aptly-titled Tapestry. The album would become the turning point in her career. Tapestry was instantly recognized as one of the landmark albums of the singer-songwriter genre of the early 1970s. With numerous hit singles, it would remain on the charts for nearly six years, selling over 10 million copies in the United States alone, and an estimated 22 million worldwide, making .

podcast.body: A blockbuster LP by Carole King, which included the deep cut "Smackwater Jack," a gently funky pop and beat track. Quincy Jones later covered this song and named his 1971 album after it, amplifying its funk and harmonica elements. "For example, in 1971, he keed into a deep cut on the back half of Carol King's blockbuster LP tapestry."

podcast.body: This album was the "longest running number one LP" of 1971. Its widespread popularity translated into a major Grammy sweep in 1972, where it won Album of the Year, with "It's Too Late" securing Record of the Year and King's composition "You've Got a Friend" winning Song of the Year. "Carol King's tapestry, the longest running number one LP of that year, swept the Grammys in 1972."
